clue.text: Pesters travellers on vacation touring Russian capital

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied of its contents, so only its two outside letters remain
to tour something is to go all round it, so the outer letters travel around the currency

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
capital in the sense of money: the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: Tourists on holiday in Moscow hassle the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian capital' points at Moscow, but capital here means money: the rouble sits inside the shell of travellers to give TROUBLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to bother or harass them, so the third-person verb is a synonym of pesters.

clue.text: Cruel Romeo's jilted Mary Jane

indicators.note: to be jilted is to be dropped by a lover, so the named letter is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: harsh treatment is cruel treatment
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A heartless Romeo has dumped a girl called Mary Jane.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Jane looks like the jilted girlfriend, but it is old slang for marijuana; take R out of HARSH to leave HASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Jane is a slang name for marijuana, and hash (hashish) is cannabis resin, so the slang terms overlap.

clue.text: Blameless conduct arising under universal agreement?

indicators.note: in a down clue, arising means the words climb upwards, so they are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal
conduct with no sin in it is blameless

explanation.surface: A question about whether faultless behaviour comes from a shared moral code everyone accepts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' places the climbing NO SIN beneath U in this down entry, so U comes first: U + NISON.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting together in complete accord, so the word is used for agreement or concord.

clue.text: RC burial conducted as per official rites

indicators.note: conducted suggests the letters are led about and directed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman Catholic funeral carried out according to the Church's proper liturgy.
explanation.walkthrough: RC is the usual abbreviation for Roman Catholic; the funeral is the anagram fodder, not the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubrics are the printed directions for conducting church services, so rubrical means following those prescribed liturgical rules.

clue.text: Monk with smoother cloak, allegedly survivor of fire

indicators.note: here with means held within the other word, as if the smoother is wrapped around the holy man

blocks.note: a lama is a Buddhist monk in Tibet
a sander is a tool for smoothing wood; cloak tells us it goes round

explanation.surface: A monk wearing the cloak of a tradesman is said to have walked out of a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allegedly' is fair because the fireproof creature is legend: medieval bestiaries claimed this amphibian could live unharmed in flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval lore claimed this amphibian was unharmed by flames, and in myth it is a spirit living in fire.

clue.text: Overcharge to spend a penny (old currency not new)

indicators.note: the pre-decimal penny symbol takes the place of the modern penny symbol, a swap of one letter for another

blocks.note: to spend a penny is a British euphemism for urinating
d was the symbol for the old pre-1971 penny
p is the symbol for the new decimal penny

explanation.surface: A complaint that it costs too much just to use a public toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend a penny' comes from the coin once needed for public toilets; swap the new-penny P in PIDDLE for the old-penny D.
explanation.definitionFit: To diddle is to swindle or cheat someone, and overcharging a customer is one way of cheating them.

clue.text: Predestined, as curate was

blocks.note: first meaning: decreed in advance by fate
second meaning: formally made a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A curate's calling was fated from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means decreed by fate or God, and also describes a priest admitted to holy orders in a church ceremony.

clue.text: Level for one river entering north-western estuary

indicators.note: entering means the first pieces go inside the later word, flowing into its mouth

blocks.note: e.g., for example, is the same as for one
R is the standard abbreviation for river
the Dee estuary lies between north Wales and the Wirral in north-west England

explanation.surface: A gauge of the water height when a river flows into a north-western estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level' looks like a water level beside the river, but it is the definition. The Dee estuary separates north Wales from the Wirral.
explanation.definitionFit: A degree is a stage or grade on a scale, as in a high degree of skill, which is a level.

clue.text: Princess in the Emirates briefly inspiring sister

indicators.note: briefly says the abbreviation is cut short, losing its final letter
to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the shortened Emirates takes the royal woman inside it

blocks.note: a rani is an Indian princess or queen
UAE is the United Arab Emirates

explanation.surface: A princess living in the Gulf is an inspiration to her sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' looks like a family relation, but the Muses were nine sisters, and Urania was the Muse of astronomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Urania was one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, daughters of Zeus who were all sisters.

clue.text: Mawkishness from son in returning embrace

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the embrace word is read from right to left
in places the son within the other word

blocks.note: a hug is an embrace
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Sentimentality as a son comes home to a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Gush is overflowing, excessive sentimental talk, which is exactly what mawkishness describes.

clue.text: Rich patron from Benin found by police in south of France

indicators.note: in places the police inside the French word for south

blocks.note: sud is the French word for south
the Garda is the police force of Ireland

explanation.surface: A wealthy benefactor from West Africa is picked up by officers on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South of France' suggests the Midi, but it means the French word for south. Benin's car registration letters keep the old name Dahomey.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar daddy is a wealthy older man who lavishes money and gifts on a younger companion, a kind of rich sponsor.

clue.text: Pop group lodged in Cotswold mansion

indicators.note: lodged in says the answer is staying inside the following words, tucked across their letters

blocks.note: surface padding that turns Pop into a pop group; it plays no part in the wordplay
the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A pop band is staying in a grand country house in the Cotswolds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop group' reads as a band, but Pop alone is the definition. The Cotswolds are hills in south-west England dotted with stately homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop and old man are both informal words for one's father, so they are interchangeable slang synonyms.

clue.text: Plays sensationalised madam's role perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given are only one possible arrangement of them

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Actors overplay the part of a brothel keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sensationalised' seems to describe how the madam is played, but it belongs to the definition: plays that are sensationalised.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a stage work with exaggerated emotion and lurid plotting, so these are dramas pitched for sensation.

clue.text: Old grottos bordering lake cut off areas of country

indicators.note: the grottos border the lake by enclosing it on every side

blocks.note: ex- means former, as in an ex-wife
grottos are small caves
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Ancient caverns beside a lake shut off whole districts of the land.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclave is a portion of a country separated from the main territory and surrounded by foreign land.

clue.text: Very large card bringing comfort in hard times

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: Drawing a big winning card cheers someone up when luck is bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation offered to someone in grief or distress, which is comfort given in hard times.

clue.text: Mark boards to form a West Country speciality

indicators.note: to board is to get on and go inside, so the mark climbs into the following words

blocks.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
to create is to form
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark sits on committees in order to set up something.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a man joining boards; M goes inside CREATE A. The West Country is south-west England, Devon and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Devon and Cornwall are famous for afternoon tea served with scones, jam and clotted cream, a regional speciality.

clue.text: Unobtrusive moves by Liberal in party succeeded

indicators.note: in sets the Liberal inside the word for a party

blocks.note: a side is a party or faction in a dispute
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A Liberal quietly manoeuvres within a party and gets ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To slide is to slip quietly or stealthily, so slides are moves made without attracting notice.

clue.text: Curb coterie from which specialised units develop

blocks.note: to stem a flow is to curb it
a cell is a small close group within an organisation

explanation.surface: Restrain the clique from which the specialist teams grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Units' sounds like military or business teams; here they are the specialised cells of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A stem cell is an undifferentiated cell that can divide and turn into the various specialised cells of an organism.

clue.text: Passionate little Dickensian changes ends

indicators.note: changes ends means the first and last letters swap places with each other

blocks.note: Little Dorrit is the title heroine of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A small Dickens character keeps switching sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' seems to describe the character's size, but it is part of the name Little Dorrit; swap her D and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrid affair is intensely hot and passionate, so the adjective is a close synonym of passionate.

clue.text: Besides catching plenty, Evans ultimately conceded bye

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the name, its final letter
something conceded is given up, so that letter is surrendered from the word for plenty
catching means holding the other word inside it

blocks.note: too means as well, besides
oodles means lots, plenty
the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A cricket report: as well as taking many catches, Evans gave away a bye.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words are a disguise: in cricket a bye is a run conceded, but here bye simply means goodbye. Godfrey Evans was an England wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-oo is a jaunty, old-fashioned British way of saying goodbye, just like the casual farewell bye.

clue.text: Special person leaving?

blocks.note: one means a person, as in one should
off means departing, as in I'm off

explanation.surface: Is someone who is going away somehow exceptional?
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is something unique, made or done only once, so the word describes a special, unrepeated thing.

clue.text: Contrary forces rapidly covering a huge distance

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the letters are read from right to left
the two words cover the answer, holding it concealed across their letters

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Opposing armies racing across a vast stretch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forces' and 'rapidly' look like words to turn into synonyms, but the answer is simply sitting backwards inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is an astronomical unit of length, about 3.26 light years, so it is an enormous distance.

clue.text: European buff

blocks.note: first meaning: from Poland
second meaning: to rub a surface until it shines

explanation.walkthrough: Buff reads as an enthusiast, a European fan, but it is the verb to shine; the capital P sense is the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish names a person from Poland, and polish as a verb means rubbing something until it gleams.

clue.text: Good-looking six-footer foolishly married short lady

indicators.note: short says the word for lady is cut, losing its last letter
foolishly suggests the letters behave in a silly, disordered way and are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A handsome tall man has unwisely wed a petite woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A six-footer sounds like a tall man, but insects have six feet; the red admiral is a common, striking butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The red admiral is a handsome black, red and white butterfly, and like all insects it has six legs.

clue.text: Britten primarily a children's composer?

blocks.note: the first letter of the name
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Britten wrote much music for children, which makes 'a children's composer' read as one phrase; the composer is the definition alone.

clue.text: Drop live commercial

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist
an ad is a commercial

explanation.definitionFit: A bead of sweat or water is a small drop, so the noun is a synonym for a droplet.

clue.text: A female halting, deeply aroused

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female
halting means limping, as a lame person walks

explanation.surface: A woman stops in her tracks, overcome with passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halting' reads as stopping, but it is the old sense of limping.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflame literally means on fire, and figuratively describes someone burning with strong emotion or passion.

clue.text: Prominent Victorian dancing ladies, one entertaining Queen

indicators.note: dancing ladies move about, so their letters shift into a new order
to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so the queen goes within

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
R is short for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Dancing ladies put on a show for Queen Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen fits the Victorian scene, but she is only one letter here. Disraeli was Queen Victoria's favourite prime minister.
